title: a foreign property read reached through an index signature needs an annotated adapter exactly as a declared one does
notes: 09-foreign-calls/foreign-property-read-needs-an-adapter pins the read of a property some declaration spells. This pins the read of one that none does: `keyed.width` resolves through a `Record<string, number>` index signature, so a rule that walks a merged property's declarations finds an empty list. An empty list of declarations is not evidence of a trust claim, and treating it as one is a fail-open — the same shape as `@throws {never}` matched per symbol, one level down. FILED HONESTLY AGAINST CURRENT BEHAVIOUR: at the time this case was written the fork accepted the program, compiled it with zero diagnostics, ran it and exited 0 printing `3`, and the xfail said so. HISTORY: the fix that was in flight landed on 2026-08-26. The prediction in this note was that the case would then score XPASS; it did not, and the reason is worth keeping. The lane closed the fail-open by deleting the fork's second gate — the one that walked the MEMBER's declarations — so the property rule now asks the receiver's provenance alone, exactly as its own comment had always claimed and as the reference does. That is the whole of what this case's SMITHERS1506 pins, and the fork now reports it at 4:17. What the fork still does not do is charge Panic to the enclosing row, so it omits the SMITHERS1101, and that is a different rule with its own standing marker. The outcome was therefore a NARROWED xfail rather than a retirement: the marker survives, the direction column changed from FAIL-OPEN to fail-closed, and the sentence in the marker that described the fail-open had to be rewritten because it had become false in the same commit that made it obsolete. Its deliberate pair is 09-foreign-calls/a-foreign-index-signature-read-through-an-element-access-needs-an-adapter, the same read spelled `keyed["width"]`, which is what shows the rule follows the receiver rather than the spelling. ON THE CASE'S OWN NAME: `…-is-refused-on-one-backend-only` describes the state this case was filed in, and it is now only half true — the READ is refused on both backends and only the row charge is one-sided. The name is kept rather than corrected because it is cited by identity from conformance/README.md, conformance/COVERAGE.md and poc/src/language/README.md, and a rename would silently dangle three citations to buy one adjective; the marker and this note carry the current state instead. Rename it only in a change that updates those citations in the same breath.

xfail.reason: NO LONGER A FAIL-OPEN. Re-measured on 2026-08-26 through `run.mjs --backend both --filter … --json`, from source rather than through `bin/smithers.js`: the fork REFUSES this program with `SMITHERS1506@4:17` — the same code at the same position as the reference — and does not run it. Its observation is `kind: diagnostics, stage: compile`; the earlier `output exit 0` printing `3` is gone. What it still omits is the `SMITHERS1101@3:1` the reference reports at the function declaration, because its property rule reports without charging Panic to the enclosing row. So BOTH BACKENDS NOW REFUSE THIS PROGRAM and the marker records a diagnostic-set divergence, not a soundness one; the direction column for this row moved from FAIL-OPEN to fail-closed on 2026-08-26. The omitted row charge is the same standing gap already recorded on 09-foreign-calls/a-callback-handed-to-an-untrusted-host-is-still-rejected and 09-foreign-calls/a-module-trust-claim-is-not-a-call-site-opt-out, and this row now retires with those two rather than on a rule of its own. WHAT CHANGED, since the marker survives and its subject did not: the fork's property rule stated in its own comment that the receiver's provenance was the rule, and then contradicted that with a second gate that walked the MEMBER's declarations — an index-signature member has none, and an empty declaration list was read as nothing to object to. That gate is gone; the rule now asks the receiver one question and covers element access, computed keys, writes, optional chains and destructuring patterns as one rule. Keep this case: it is the only row that would notice the second gate coming back.
xfail.doc: specification/compatibility.mdx, "Foreign Boundary": "Calling an unannotated foreign runtime value MUST add the checked `panic` case, because JavaScript and TypeScript may throw, reject, or violate a declaration." A getter reached through an index signature is such a call, and an index signature is a declaration of the CONTAINER, never a trust claim about the member.
